text: The composite includes objectively recorded death and a protocol-defined BPD component at 36 weeks PMA
finding: Endpoint and time supported; objective recording described as not directly established, a conservative qualification rather than global falsity.

text: BPD criteria incorporate oxygen/respiratory-support thresholds after at least 28 days of support; where oxygen need is subjective, an oxygen-reduction test confirms dependency using an oxygen-saturation threshold
finding: BPD thresholds and subjective oxygen-dependency testing correctly attributed to appendix p14 and main p3.

text: This is a structured, clinically relevant method for the outcome, though the BPD component requires some clinical judgment and the protocol does not establish external validation for this exact trial implementation
finding: Structured/clinically relevant characterization accepted as reasonable; however, denial of support for some clinical judgment is a false alarm on a qualified inference from the explicit subjective oxygen-need statement. External-validation scope is appropriately limited.

text: The evidence therefore supports probably not inappropriate.
finding: The final RoB interpretation is not separately classified. No replacement judgment requested or produced; count this unit transparently rather than as an implicit pass.

text: The oxygen-reduction test flowchart was not visually inspectable in the tool response; the applicable textual criteria were inspected.
finding: Tool/image-inspection uncertainty cannot be verified from text spans, correctly retained.

text: The same 36-week assessment point, BPD criteria, and oxygen-reduction approach apply to both randomized groups; trial personnel and outcome assessors were blinded
finding: Common approach accepted as inference, not explicit group-specific fact; blinding support found in main p2, which is exported for the assessor-awareness claim rather than bound to this differential warrant. Original per-claim citation mismatch is not explicitly distinguished.

text: For eligible infants, oxygen-reduction testing was not performed in similar proportions (13/86 vs 13/94)
finding: Known numeric clause correctly classified as not established by supplied citations; no claim that the counts are globally false. Proportion-similarity interpretation is not separately evaluated.

text: No group-specific threshold or assessment method is reported
finding: Qualifies the absence of group-specific method wording without asserting contradiction; no global proof of equivalence.

text: This supports probably no differential measurement; the exact assessment opportunity for every participant is not fully detailed.
finding: Assessment opportunity is correctly left unestablished; differential-measurement conclusion is only indirectly addressed through common approach inference.

text: Outcome information was unavailable for some participants and reasons for all missing oxygen assessments are not fully reported; this relates chiefly to D3 availability rather than showing differential measurement.
finding: Reasons for missing oxygen assessments left unexplained; availability and D3/D4 domain-allocation clauses are not individually evaluated.

text: The report states that the persons assessing outcomes were unaware of randomization assignments
finding: Assessor-blinding statement accurately supported by article p2 lines68-70.

text: This addresses assessor awareness directly; it does not rely solely on the endpoint being objective.
finding: Direct assessor-awareness rationale accepted as fair description.

text: The protocol states that an SAP would be developed before the first participant was randomized and that final amendments would be completed before unblinding
finding: DAPA protocol planning requirement correctly supported, without converting it into proof of compliance.

text: The applicable SAP (edition 3.0, dated 23 July 2019) prespecifies this time-to-first primary composite and its Cox-model hazard ratio analysis, and the report says the trial was conducted and reported according to the protocol and SAP
finding: SAP date, endpoint and reported protocol/SAP adherence addressed; Cox prespecification attribution is separately qualified under the multiple-analyses warrant, not fully split here.

text: The article's reported primary analysis follows the planned ITT, adjudicated-endpoint approach and reports the planned HR/CI
finding: Actual HR/CI and ITT supported, adjudication conduct correctly not inferred as directly confirmed solely from SAP plan.

text: This supports prespecification before unblinding; exact investigator access timing is not separately documented.
finding: Before-unblinding prespecification treated as inference from protocol commitment with timing uncertainty retained.

text: The exact date of finalization of SAP edition 3.0 relative to unblinded outcome data access is not directly stated in the SAP header, although the protocol commits to final amendments before unblinding.
finding: Exact finalization/data-access timing uncertainty explicitly preserved.

text: The protocol and SAP define the primary measurement as the time to first event in the composite of cardiovascular death, HF hospitalization, or urgent HF visit
finding: Primary time-to-first composite correctly supported by SAP p241.

text: They distinguish component analyses and a separate secondary composite; the report identifies and reports the prespecified primary composite and its components
finding: Outcome distinction addressed, but locator p5 lines42-55 is secondary/recurrent-result text, not the primary component-result passage at p5 lines27-38. This is a source-range attribution defect despite support elsewhere in the supplied p5 span.

text: There is no evidence that a different eligible primary definition or time point was selected based on results.
finding: No-selection statement explicitly limited to supplied spans, not direct proof or contradiction.

text: The SAP specifies the primary time-to-first-event analysis using an ITT full analysis set and a Cox model stratified by diabetes status and adjusted for prior HF hospitalization, with HR and 95% CI reported
finding: Additional real attribution gap detected: selected SAP p241 does not specify Cox stratification/adjustment; article p4 specifies performed model, not this SAP prespecification.

text: The article reports that the trial followed its SAP and describes the same ITT Cox approach
finding: Reported adherence and performed ITT/Cox method correctly grounded in main p2/p4.

text: Other component, secondary, recurrent-event, and subgroup analyses are separately identified; there is no evidence the primary numerical result was chosen from eligible alternatives based on results.
finding: Secondary/recurrent analyses and results-driven-selection inference addressed across the selection paragraphs; separately reported subgroup analysis clause not explicitly checked.
